policy_name: Purchase Order and Payment Approval Limits
content:
Approval limits by role and amount:
- Store Manager: GBP 5,000
- Warehouse Manager: GBP 10,000
- Buyer: GBP 50,000
- Category Manager: GBP 100,000
- Director: GBP 500,000
- CFO/CEO: unlimited
All orders over GBP 1,000 require 2 approvals. All supplier bank detail changes require Finance review.

Put customer on credit hold when:
- Invoice >60 days overdue
- Account balance >GBP 500k
- DSO >90 days
Action: stop shipments, escalate to Credit Controller, contact customer. Release after payment received or payment plan agreed.

For quality non-conformances:
1. High-risk defects (safety, functionality): Immediate hold on all POs. Require corrective action plan within 5 days.
2. Medium-risk defects (cosmetic, minor): Limit POs to 50% of normal volume. Require action plan within 10 days.
3. Low-risk defects (documentation): Monitor and notify supplier within 15 days.
Suspend supplier if repeated issues (>3 in 12 months). Exit if corrective action not implemented within 30 days.

Currency hedging limits:
- USD exposure: hedge 50-80% of 12-month forecast. Max 100%.
- EUR exposure: hedge 40-70% of 12-month forecast. Max 90%.
- Other major currencies: hedge 40-60%. Max 80%.
Instruments allowed: forward contracts, options (call spreads max). Forbid: speculative positions, exotic options.
Review hedge ratios quarterly. Spot rates used for P&L; mark hedges at forward rates.

All suppliers must maintain:
- General Liability: min GBP 2m (high-risk) or GBP 500k (low-risk)
- Product Liability: min GBP 5m (food/apparel) or GBP 1m (other)
- Cyber Liability: min GBP 1m (if data access)
- Cargo Insurance: min 110% of shipment value
- All policies: evidence of coverage required at onboarding and annually

Requirements by risk tier:
HIGH-RISK (emerging markets, new sector, high spend):
- Social and ethical audit (BSCI or equivalent) required before first order
- Business registration and tax ID verification
- Bank references (3 suppliers)
- Insurance evidence (GL 2m+, PL 5m+)
- Sanctions screening required
MEDIUM-RISK (developed market, established sector):
- Audit within 12 months of first order
- Business registration verification
- Bank references (2 suppliers)
- Insurance evidence (GL 1m+, PL 2m+)
LOW-RISK (existing supplier, low spend):
- Basic compliance check
- Insurance verification
- Annual audit if spend >GBP 500k

Inventory ownership: Transfer of title at receipt into our DC (not in-transit). In-transit goods remain supplier's responsibility until gate-in.
Status definitions:
- Available: ready for picking or sale
- In-transit: on PO, not yet received
- Reserved: allocated to open orders
- Damaged: non-saleable, awaiting write-off approval
Valuation: FIFO method. Seasonal stock over 180 days old to be marked down 25% minimum per NRV rules.

When allegations of forced labour or serious violations arise:
1. IMMEDIATE (within 24 hours): Escalate to General Counsel and Ethics Officer. Secure evidence.
2. WITHIN 5 DAYS: Assess credibility (review original reporting, NGO corroboration, supply chain connection). Interview factory if credible.
3. WITHIN 10 DAYS: Decide on hold/suspension/exit. Communicate decision to affected functions (Sourcing, Finance, Supply Chain).
Do NOT communicate to media or public without Legal approval.
Document all steps and findings for regulatory response.

Liability caps:
- Our position: No cap on product liability, safety claims. Cap at 2x annual order value for other claims.
- First fallback: Cap at order value.
- Red line: Will not accept cap <order value.
IP Ownership:
- Our position: We own all IP including improvements and know-how.
- First fallback: Shared IP rights; we get license to use at no cost.
- Red line: Will not accept supplier retaining exclusive rights.
Force majeure:
- Our position: Force majeure only for unforeseeable events; requires suspension, not termination.
- First fallback: Allow termination if event lasts >90 days.
- Red line: None; event must clear before resuming.

QUALITY INCIDENT:
- Severity 1 (safety): Immediate hold, exec escalation, customer notification within 4 hours
- Severity 2 (functionality): 24-hour response, manager escalation, customer notification within 24 hours
- Severity 3 (cosmetic): 5-day response, team escalation
SUPPLY CHAIN INCIDENT (geopolitical, transport, supplier failure):
- Tier 1 (affects delivery <72 hours): Escalate to VP Supply Chain immediately
- Tier 2 (affects delivery 3-7 days): Manager escalation, sourcing team response
- Tier 3 (future impact): Monitor and document
SECURITY INCIDENT:
- CISO involvement mandatory. Supplier user account compromise: lock account, block payments, audit access logs.

policy_name: Legal Guidance on Admissions and Claims Wording
content:
Avoid in customer communication, marketing, and internal documents:
- 'Defect' or 'defective' (use 'does not meet spec' or 'variation')
- 'We are responsible for...' (use 'The matter involves...')
- Admitting causation without evidence ('caused by X' without testing)
- Making comparative claims ('better than competitor') without substantiation
- Sustainability claims ('eco-friendly', 'sustainable') without certification
SAFE WORDING:
- 'We are investigating the matter.'
- 'Testing to date indicates...'
- 'Meets ISO 14040 environmental standards.'
- Always include: 'Pending further testing/investigation/legal review.'

policy_name: Lot Acceptance Quality and Release Policy
content:
AQL (Acceptable Quality Level) by defect severity:
- Critical (safety, function): AQL 0.65%, max 1 defect per 100 units sampled
- Major (appearance >2cm, function <spec): AQL 1.5%, max 2 defects per 100 units
- Minor (small appearance): AQL 2.5%, max 3 defects per 100 units
Release decision:
- Results within AQL: Release for sale
- 1 critical defect: Reject entire lot. Request rework or replacement.
- >1 major defect: Conditional release at 20% price reduction if customer accepts
- Sorted and reworked lots: Retest at 2x sample size. All critical defects must be zero.

policy_name: Internal Policy on Market Entry Structures
content:
Market entry structures by region and spend:
UK/EU (mature markets, <GBP 5m annual): Franchise or partnership preferred. Subsidiary if >GBP 50m spend or IP at risk.
Emerging markets (China, India, SE Asia, <GBP 20m): Joint venture with local partner required. IP strictly protected. Exit clause mandatory.
Nearshore (Turkey, Morocco, Mexico, GBP 5-50m): Joint venture or subsidiary. Build IP gradually; don't over-rely on one partner.
Exit: Subsidiary - require 6-month notice, transfer of contracts and staff obligations. JV - buyout clause if partner underperforms.

Assurance requirements for ESG and sustainability reporting:
Scope 1 & 2 Emissions: Annual independent third-party assurance (ISO 14064-3). Acceptable assurance providers: ISAE 3000 accredited bodies.
Scope 3 Emissions: Reasonable assurance required for supply chain emissions >50% of total. Data evidence: supplier questionnaires, shipment records, conversion factors from GHG Protocol.
Supply Chain Disclosures: Annual audit of forced labour due diligence (legal obligation UK MSA 2015). Evidence: supplier audit reports, sanctions screening, grievance records.
Reporting Framework Compliance: All disclosures against TCFD, GRI, SASB standards require management review and sign-off.

policy_name: Supplier Code of Conduct - Wage and Hour Clauses
content:
Mandatory clauses in supplier code of conduct:
MINIMUM WAGES: Suppliers must pay at least local legal minimum wage or industry standard (whichever is higher) plus statutory benefits.
WORKING HOURS: Maximum 48 hours per week normal working hours, max 60 hours including overtime. Overtime voluntary and fairly compensated (at least 1.5x regular rate).
FREE TIME: Minimum one rest day per 7 days, plus statutory public holidays.
CHILD LABOUR: No workers under 15 (or local school-leaving age). Under 18s not permitted in hazardous work.
FORCED LABOUR: Zero tolerance. No wage deductions except legal requirements. All work voluntary.
FREEDOM OF ASSOCIATION: Workers may join or form unions; suppliers must not interfere or discriminate.
